message.content:
**Proteins commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|-------------------------| | **Integral (Trans‑Membrane)** | Span the bilayer; form pores/transport pathways or signal transduction sites. | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Glucose transporter GLUT1 / GLUT4
• Aquaporin‑1
• Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv11.1
• G‑protein–coupled receptors (e.g., β₂‑adrenergic)
• Connexin43 (gap junctions)
• Caveolin‑1 (caveolae scaffold) | | **Peripheral (Non‑integral)** | Attach loosely to one side of the membrane via electrostatic interactions or through other proteins. | • Actin‑binding proteins (ezrin, radixin, moesin – ERM family)
• Annexins (bind phospholipids in Ca²⁺‑dependent manner)
• Integrins (link extracellular matrix to actin cytoskeleton)
• Cadherins (homophilic adhesion molecules) | | **Lipid‑anchored** | Covalently attached to lipids embedded in the outer leaflet. | • Squalene synthase (prenylation)
• Hedgehog signaling components (cholesterol‑modified)
• Ras isoforms (farnesylated/GDP‑bound) | | **Extracellular domain proteins** | Often serve as receptors or binding partners outside the cell. | • Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)
• Insulin receptor
• Toll‑like receptor 4 (TLR4) | ### Quick Takeaways * **Integral proteins** cross the hydrophobic core—think ion channels, pumps, GPCRs. * **Peripheral proteins** sit on the surface, often linking the membrane to the cytoskeleton or participating in signaling cascades. * Many membrane proteins have both domains (extracellular ligand‑binding + intracellular signaling). These lists are far from exhaustive—the mammalian plasma membrane contains thousands of distinct proteins—but they cover the most frequently cited families encountered in textbooks and research literature.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They likely expect an answer listing some common types or examples of proteins located in the plasma membrane.

We can provide general categories and examples: integral (transmembrane) like ion channels, transporters; peripheral proteins like receptors, enzymes, cytoskeletal attachments etc. Provide examples such as Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptor, integrin, cadherin, connexin, aquaporin, hemagglutinin, etc. Also mention lipid rafts with caveolin, flotillin. Could also refer to human proteome data sets but not necessary.
